business_problem: The Standard needed better visibility into IT and cloud spending because spreadsheet-based planning and a legacy ERP system made it hard to explain costs, prioritize funding, and manage portfolio delivery across digital-transformation work.
solution_summary: The Standard rebuilt its technology-finance operating model around IBM Apptio, IBM Cloudability, and IBM Targetprocess. Apptio became the core financial-planning layer, with the TBM taxonomy codified into Workday ERP so IT spending could be segmented and explained in business-friendly terms instead of account codes and spreadsheet tabs. Cloudability added cloud cost visibility and rightsizing analysis, especially across a rapidly growing Azure footprint, while Targetprocess gave delivery teams a common operating picture for project, product, portfolio, and resource management in both Agile and waterfall environments. Together, those tools linked cost transparency, cloud governance, and delivery execution so the company could shift spending toward strategic initiatives, measure say-do performance, and manage acquisition integration with tighter financial control. The result is a connected planning and delivery stack rather than isolated budgeting, cloud, and portfolio tools.

solution_components.name: IBM Apptio
solution_components.role: Provides the IT financial-planning and TBM model used to analyze, forecast, and communicate technology spending.

solution_components.name: IBM Cloudability
solution_components.role: Delivers cloud-spend visibility and rightsizing insights for the company's Azure environment.

solution_components.name: IBM Targetprocess
solution_components.role: Aligns portfolios, programs, projects, and delivery teams around shared priorities and resource planning.

data_flow: ERP and financial data feed Apptio for business-friendly cost modeling, cloud-usage data is analyzed in Cloudability for optimization opportunities, and portfolio commitments and delivery status move through Targetprocess so leaders can connect spend, capacity, and execution decisions.
business_outcome: The Standard improved cost transparency, redirected more IT-finance effort toward decision support, optimized cloud spending, and increased planning and delivery discipline across its transformation portfolio.
